mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during war-related demand shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of high wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during supply chain disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by more than 0.3% in the same month indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise by >0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of high wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 4% for four consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and higher consumption, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high savings rates.
